unreg:all_star_exhibition_games.reviewer: independent-reviewer-NBA (Claude agent, agent verification, not human expert)
unreg:all_star_exhibition_games.rederivation_notes: My chain, derived from the three Kalshi rule texts before opening the record: (1) roster formation and replacement (selection, nationality or draft assignment, late injury replacements); (2) who plays and for how long in 12-minute games or target races, with effort as a regime variable; (3) offence-only scoring strength per team; (4) single-game conversion, a timed margin with large SD for KXNBAALLSTARGAME versus a first-passage race to 40 then 25 for KXNBARISINGSTARS; (5) tournament structure, namely Game-1-dependent pairings, a 1-1-1 point-differential tiebreak, a final; (6) settlement on the announced champion, with postponement via 'originally scheduled for'. Required inputs: format ledger, roster strength, minutes plan, effort/variance baseline, race model, path simulation, injury vintages. The record matches this chain and goes further on seat asymmetry and shrinkage. Differences found: the strength-to-margin scale is fitted on pooled formats, the 2025 format is assumed rather than researched, and the catalog lost the per-series scope.

findings.text: nba.asg_roster_strength_composite converts the team gap to expected margin per 12 minutes with one scale factor fitted on 'past exhibition margins (2013-2025, pooled over formats)'. Its own stage s4 and interaction 1 say timed and target regimes must be estimated separately and margin SD depends on game length; 2013-2024 All-Star Games were long conventional games. The pooled fit and the 'per 12 minutes' unit are not defined, so the main primary input cannot be computed as written.

The 2025 KXNBAALLSTAR format (drafted teams plus a Rising Stars winner as fourth team, target-score races) is used as fact in path_sim rationale, nba.target_score_race_model why and the KXNBAALLSTAR input scope, yet the same record says Kalshi's text gives no format and gap e2 says the 2025 format was not researched. nba.target_score_race_model free_sources also cites '2024-2025 All-Star target games'; I believe the 2024 game was conventional, which I could not verify here. Scope for KXNBAALLSTAR rests on an unresearched format.

Rising Stars is described as 'untimed' with 'no clock' in the race model; the sampled rule says only 'first team to reach or exceed 40 points'. A time limit or overtime rule is not excluded by the text; it should be a CONTRACT_AMBIGUOUS item.

Catalog entry for the archetype has no per-series scope (series field is None on all 18 inputs) although the record's series_input_scope differs per ticker (nationality quota only for the 2026 game, Rising Stars strength only for KXNBARISINGSTARS); catalog target/label also mention a 'legends game' for which no series exists, and contract_types holds a near-duplicate 'NBA All-Star game'.

unreg:all_star_game_mvp.reviewer: independent-reviewer-NBA (Claude agent, agent verification, not human expert)
unreg:all_star_game_mvp.rederivation_notes: My chain from the single KXNBAALLSTARMVP rule text: (1) participation, since non-participation resolves No, so P(Yes) <= P(plays); (2) the player's team result in the multi-game tournament; (3) the player's individual scoring line under capped 12-minute games and shared minutes; (4) a voted award decided by a small media panel plus a fan share, so narrative and recency matter; (5) settlement on the official announcement with selector, scope and co-winner handling unstated in the rule. Required inputs: withdrawal/replacement hazard for All-Star selectees, tournament path simulation, minutes and usage, vote model, fan-vote data, format ledger. The record follows this chain closely. Differences: vote arithmetic and weights are stated as rules despite unverified sourcing, the two vote inputs are circular, the withdrawal hazard is calibrated on the wrong population, and a pre-2026 format claim conflicts with the sibling record.

findings.text: Vote facts are internally inconsistent and presented as the '2026 rule': stage s4 says about 14 votes 'including the fan component', while the settlement text and gap m1 say 10 of 14 panel votes with the media/fan split not given; nba.asg_mvp_vote_model asserts 0.75 panel + 0.25 fan and 'scope = whole tournament' without a provenance flag, and nba.asg_mvp_fan_vote_share falls back to placeholder weights a=1,b=2,c=0.3 and assumes per-player fan-vote returns are 'published', which is not shown and is not declared DATA_UNAVAILABLE.

nba.asg_mvp_vote_model and nba.asg_mvp_fan_vote_share are circular: the model's final score is 0.75 x panel + 0.25 x fan_share, and fan_share's MVP score uses the panel share from the model; both use tournament points share. They are two primary inputs that cannot be computed independently. The conditional-logit fit 'on 20+ events' with five or more covariates and one three-game-tournament edition is also under-identified and not disclosed as a gap.

nba.asw_field_withdrawal_hazard is calibrated on withdrawals from 3PT/dunk/skills fields 2010-2026 ('sponsor negotiation', announcement weeks ahead). The MVP clause needs P(an All-Star selectee does not play), a different population with its own replacement process. The shared input gives the wrong base rate for the cap on every Yes price.

The variant 'before 2026 the All-Star Game was a single game' (also gap m2) conflicts with the sibling record, which treats KXNBAALLSTAR 2025 ('Shaq's OGs', a named drafted team) as a multi-team format. If 2025 was already a tournament, the comparability and sample-size statements for earlier MVPs are wrong. Not verified either way from Kalshi text.

Interaction voting_narrative x tournament path ('lopsided final makes the panel weigh the whole tournament') is a speculation with no evidence or measurable regime variable; the catalog entry carries no per-series scope.

unreg:all_star_weekend_events.reviewer: independent-reviewer-NBA (Claude agent, agent verification, not human expert)
unreg:all_star_weekend_events.rederivation_notes: My chain from the 3PT, dunk and Shooting Stars rule texts: (1) field and withdrawal, with No on withdrawal for individual contests; (2) per-entrant skill under no defence: rack make rates and release tempo inside 70 s, dunk repertoire and make risk, and for Shooting Stars a three-player team shooting a circuit of spots of different values; (3) format aggregation, namely top-three advancement then a final that resets scores, two dunk rounds with two finalists, top-two of four teams then a final; (4) judging for dunks; (5) tie procedures; (6) settlement on the announced winner. Required inputs: format ledger with provenance, 3PT score PMF, shooting transfer, dunk judge model, team skill for every spot type, withdrawal hazard. Differences found: Shooting Stars includes two-point spots that no input can estimate, catalog text still references departed series, and 'verified' labels rest on search relays.

findings.text: Shooting Stars spots (per evidence_zblk/NBA_u10_shooting_stars.json) include a layup/dunk, an 18-ft baseline, an elbow and top of the key, all 2-point spots; yet nba.shooting_stars_team_skill takes spot make rates from nba.threept_spot_and_tempo_profile (3PT racks, 3PA locations, 27+ ft rate) and legends' 3P% and FT%. No input supplies rim-finishing, mid-range or elbow skill, so even with the rules PDF read the team model cannot be estimated. This is missing catalog content, not only source access.

Residue of departed series in the catalog entry: per-input series lists still name KXNBAALLSTARGAME, KXNBAALLSTAR, KXNBARISINGSTARS and KXNBAALLSTARMVP on seven inputs (format ledger, injuries_pit, news, rule_change_pipeline, calendar_announcements, m.rules_text, m.settlement_truth); m.rules_text why still cites 'the 12-minute round robin and 40/25 targets'; rule_change_pipeline why says 'for the Game and contests'; variant 11 still cites Rising Stars. The split did not clean the input-to-series assignment.

nba.shooting_stars_team_skill labels the 2026 format fields 'VERIFIED' (70 s, seven spots, top two, higher final score wins). The evidence file says these are quoted fragments or paraphrases returned by a search tool, never read from the release or rules PDF. My own search reached only summaries and again gave the final-round tie as 'replayed', unchanged from the conflicting-sources state. The label overstates the evidence.

Stage s5 and the rationale call the four Shooting Stars teams 'franchise-named'; the evidence file lists Team All-Star, Team Knicks, Team Cameron and Team Harper, so only one is franchise-named. The u8 residual (game_side blueprint and three disjoint processes in one record) is honestly disclosed and left open.

player_points.reviewer: independent-reviewer-NBA (Claude agent, agent verification, not human expert)
player_points.rederivation_notes: My chain from KXNBAPTS and KXNBAPTSPROT rule texts: availability and minutes scenarios (inactive or never-entering voids at a fair price; PROT also refunds first-half-only appearances unless the strike is met); possessions on court; usage share given the five-man unit and teammate absence; shot quality and conversion against scheme; free-throw trips; game-script truncation or overtime; nested-rung monotonicity and the upper tail; settlement. Required inputs: minutes mixture, injury vintages, exit hazard, usage allocation, shot-type expected points, FT rate, blowout curve from ratings, dispersion. The record matches this and its quoted rule text is verbatim. Differences: the bench re-filing rests on a claim about Kalshi terms that live evidence contradicts, and bench or departed-series residue remains in input texts and the catalog.

findings.text: The re-filing of KXNBABENCHPTS is justified in settlement_definition and the evidence file as 'BASKETBALLENTITYSTAT terms make it a team-entity stat, not a player stat'. Live Kalshi series API (2026-11-09): KXNBAPTS (scope 'Player Points') and KXNBAREB (scope 'Player Rebounds') use the same BASKETBALLENTITYSTAT.pdf; team head-to-head uses BASKETBALLH2H and team totals BASKETBALLTOTALS. So the terms template is the player-prop template and cannot support a team reading. The filing rests only on the title/scope string 'Bench Points', with no market ever listed.

Stale bench and departed-series text remains: new_inputs nba.cross_player_points_dependence why says 'Still needed for the bench total'; input_audit nba.stat_dist reason cites 'the bench-total sum' and m.rules_text 'the bench definition'; in the catalog, cross_player_points_dependence why still says 'KXNBAH2H*, PRA-type and leader contracts in this archetype', points_upper_tail_rate says 'prices KXNBAESCALATORPTS', and nba.combo_component_marginals is still attached as primary for PRA/PR/PA/H2H-PRA although the audit sets it IRRELEVANT and no patch detaches it.

Market-derived inputs remain as drivers in the catalog contrary to the record's own audit: nba.garbage (spread-driven blowout probability) is primary, nba.implied_team_totals and m.external_lines secondary, with interactions [garbage x minutes] and [pace x implied_team_totals], while input_audit marks all three BENCHMARK_ONLY and no archetype_patches role change exists. The market-free replacement (nba.rating_blowout_minutes_curve) is present, but the benchmark inputs still carry driver roles.

Internal contradiction: variants_and_edge_cases[2] says KXNBABENCHPTS 'is a team sum over non-starters', while gap pp-bucket-mixing says a player-level reading cannot be excluded. Also KXNBAPTSPROT uses a different terms PDF (NBAENTITYSTATCOVERED) from KXNBAPTS, which weakens the stated assumption that its inactive/postponement wording matches KXNBAPTS, and the phrase 'Source Agencies referred to in the full rules' does not appear in the sampled text.

game_overtime_and_team_events.reviewer: independent-reviewer-NBA (Claude agent, agent verification, not human expert)
game_overtime_and_team_events.rederivation_notes: My chain: P(OT) is the mass of the regulation-margin distribution at zero, set by the expected margin (own ratings, not the spread), margin SD, and an excess factor from end-of-game tie-forcing; overtime length and count; for KXNBASERIESOT a count threshold over a random series length with within-series dependence; bench points as bench minutes (240 plus 25 per overtime, minus starter minutes) times bench scoring rate, with the starter designation defining who counts; team three-point head-to-head as a difference of two correlated counts with 50/50 ties. Required inputs: lineup-adjusted ratings, tie PMF, tie-forcing policy, OT period distribution, series model, bench minute and rate models, starter ledger, pair-difference model. I verified the Gaussian arithmetic (3.3, 2.3, 1.7 percent) and the tie-mass estimates. The record matches. Differences: KXNBABENCHPTS is treated as a known team total on unsupported evidence, and benchmark inputs keep driver roles in the catalog.

findings.text: KXNBABENCHPTS is described as a 'team Bench Points total' and 'team-entity terms' that differ from the head-to-head terms (settlement_definition, variants[14], gap u8, nba.team_bench_points_model why). Live Kalshi data shows BASKETBALLENTITYSTAT is the player-prop template (KXNBAPTS, KXNBAREB), no market has ever been listed, and the scope string 'Bench Points' carries no team qualifier. Both the entity (team or player) and the strike construction are unknown, yet nba.team_bench_points_model is a primary input defined for a team total.

Market-derived inputs keep driver roles in the catalog although input_audit marks them BENCHMARK_ONLY: m.external_lines is primary ('the sharp sportsbook number is the benchmark prior'), nba.garbage secondary and nba.score_resid/nba.ot_model carry spread-keyed definitions; the interaction [nba.bench_scoring x nba.garbage] and [m.rules_text x nba.ot_model] remain in the catalog.

Four inputs estimate the same bench-points quantity (nba.bench_scoring, nba.bench_minutes_distribution, nba.starter_bench_definition_ledger, nba.team_bench_points_model, whose why says the others 'only describe in parts'); the overlap is not resolved as DUPLICATE. category_coverage.settlement_contract note says 'All five series have rules text' after the record was widened to six; nba.reg_tie_pmf_model cites a non-existent input id 'nba.margin sd model'.
